summary: This bill prohibits the Department of Homeland Security from establishing new immigration processing or detention facilities without first publishing a public notice for comments, securing a written agreement with state and local officials, and providing advance notice to Congress.

scores.thoughts: This bill directly addresses the construction and operation of new immigration processing sites and detention centers by requiring public comment, agreements with local officials, and congressional notification. This makes immigration a central theme of the bill.

The bill imposes new procedural requirements for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) when constructing, acquiring, renovating, or operating new facilities. While it doesn't directly appropriate funds, these requirements could indirectly affect the cost and timeline of DHS projects, thus having a minor impact on government spending related to infrastructure.

The bill requires public notices for new facilities to include information on compliance with applicable environmental regulations and an engineering review addressing waste exportation, water usage, and electrical demand. This indicates a moderate, though not primary, focus on environmental considerations related to these facilities.
